content_snippet_create_request.title: Create Content Snippet Request
content_snippet_create_request.description: The request payload for creating a content snippet. You can provide either `json_blocks` or `body_markdown` for the snippet content — they are mutually exclusive. When `json_blocks` is omitted or `null` and `body_markdown` is omitted or blank, the snippet is created with a single empty paragraph.

title.description: The title of the content snippet. The API accepts a missing, `null` or empty title.

json_blocks.description: The content blocks that make up the body of the snippet. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.

body_markdown.description: The content of the snippet in markdown. An alternative to `json_blocks` — you can provide content as markdown instead of structured blocks. Mutually exclusive with `json_blocks`.

locale.description: The locale of the content snippet. Defaults to `en`.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to target this content snippet to for Fin AI Agent. Pass an empty array or omit the field for no audience targeting. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.

ai_chatbot_availability.description: Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). Defaults to true.

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Copilot. Defaults to true.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Sales Agent. Defaults to true.

content_snippet_update_request.title: Update Content Snippet Request
content_snippet_update_request.description: The request payload for updating a content snippet. All fields are optional — only provided fields will be updated. `json_blocks` and `body_markdown` are mutually exclusive.

title.description: The title of the content snippet.

json_blocks.description: The content blocks that make up the body of the snippet. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.

body_markdown.description: The content of the snippet in markdown. An alternative to `json_blocks` — you can provide content as markdown instead of structured blocks. Mutually exclusive with `json_blocks`.

locale.description: The locale of the content snippet.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to target this content snippet to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged (PATCH semantics). Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.

ai_chatbot_availability.description: Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin).

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Copilot.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the content snippet should be available for AI Sales Agent.

dynamic_content.title: Dynamic Content
dynamic_content.description: Dynamic content is a reusable piece of content that you can insert into Help Center articles. It holds one variation per locale, and optionally per brand.

type.description: String representing the object's type. Always has the value `dynamic_content`.

id.description: The unique identifier for the dynamic content.

name.description: The name of the dynamic content. Returned HTML-escaped, for example `&` as `&`.

key.description: The identifier that articles use to reference the dynamic content. Derived from the name when the dynamic content is created, and never changes.

content_type.description: Whether the dynamic content is a short inline value (`inline`) or one or more blocks of content (`block`).

default_locale.description: The locale whose variation is used when there's no variation for the requested locale.

variations.description: The variations of the dynamic content.

created_at.description: The time the dynamic content was created as a Unix timestamp.

updated_at.description: The time the dynamic content was last updated as a Unix timestamp.

dynamic_content_variation.title: Dynamic Content Variation
dynamic_content_variation.description: The value of a dynamic content for one locale, and optionally one brand.

type.description: String representing the object's type. Always has the value `dynamic_content_variation`.

id.description: The unique identifier for the variation.

brand_id.description: The unique identifier for the brand the variation applies to. `null` for a variation that applies to all brands.

text_content.description: The value of an inline variation. `null` for block dynamic content.

json_blocks.description: The content blocks of a block variation. `null` for inline dynamic content.

intentionally_empty.description: Whether the variation is intentionally empty. An intentionally empty variation shows nothing instead of falling back to the default content, and has an empty `text_content` or `json_blocks`.

created_at.description: The time the variation was created as a Unix timestamp.

updated_at.description: The time the variation was last updated as a Unix timestamp.

dynamic_content_list.title: Dynamic Content List
dynamic_content_list.description: A paginated list of dynamic content.

data.description: An array of dynamic content objects.

total_count.description: The total number of dynamic content.

per_page.description: The number of results per page.

dynamic_content_variation_request.title: Dynamic Content Variation Request
dynamic_content_variation_request.description: A variation of a dynamic content. Provide `text_content` for inline dynamic content, or `body` for block dynamic content.

locale.description: The locale of the variation. Each locale can appear once per brand.

brand_id.description: The unique identifier for the brand the variation applies to. Omit for a variation that applies to all brands.

text_content.description: The value of an inline variation.

body.description: The content of a block variation in HTML.

intentionally_empty.description: Set to `true` to make the variation show nothing instead of falling back to the default content. Any `text_content` or `body` sent with it is ignored.

dynamic_content_create_request.title: Create Dynamic Content Request
dynamic_content_create_request.description: The request payload for creating dynamic content.

name.description: The name of the dynamic content. Must be unique in the workspace.

content_type.description: Whether the dynamic content is a short inline value (`inline`) or one or more blocks of content (`block`). Can't be changed later.

default_locale.description: The locale whose variation is used when there's no variation for the requested locale. `variations` must include a variation for this locale that applies to all brands.

variations.description: The variations of the dynamic content, one per locale and optionally per brand. Set `brand_id` on a variation to override the all-brands value for that brand. At least one is required.

dynamic_content_update_request.title: Update Dynamic Content Request
dynamic_content_update_request.description: The request payload for updating dynamic content. All fields are optional — only provided fields are updated.

name.description: The name of the dynamic content. Must be unique in the workspace. Renaming doesn't change the `key`.

default_locale.description: The locale whose variation is used when there's no variation for the requested locale. The dynamic content must have a variation for this locale that applies to all brands.

variations.description: The full set of variations. Existing variations that aren't included are deleted.

content_search_default_item.description: The flat result shape returned from Knowledge Hub search for content snippets, external pages, uploaded files, and internal articles.

conversation_list_item.description: The data returned about your conversations when you list or search them.

id.description: The id representing the conversation.

title.description: The title given to the conversation.

created_at.description: The time the conversation was created.

updated_at.description: The last time the conversation was updated.

waiting_since.description: The last time a Contact responded to an Admin. In other words, the time a customer started waiting for a response. Set to null if last reply is from an Admin.

snoozed_until.description: If set this is the time in the future when this conversation will be marked as open. i.e. it will be in a snoozed state until this time. i.e. it will be in a snoozed state until this time.

admin_assignee_id.description: The id of the admin assigned to the conversation. If it's not assigned to an admin it will return 0.

team_assignee_id.description: The id of the team assigned to the conversation. If it's not assigned to a team it will return 0.

company.description: The company associated with the conversation.

ai_agent_participated.description: Indicates whether the AI Agent participated in the conversation.

sales_agent_participated.description: Indicates whether the Sales Agent participated in the conversation.

channel.description: The channel through which the conversation was initiated and its current channel.

topics.description: The topics of the conversation. An empty object when the workspace doesn't use topics.

id.description: The id of the topic.

total_count.description: The number of topics.

ticket.description: The ticket details when the conversation is a ticket. `null` for any other conversation.

id.description: The id of the ticket's conversation.

url.description: The link to the ticket in the inbox.

custom_attributes.description: The ticket's attributes, keyed by attribute name.

type.description: The data type of the attribute.

state.description: The current state of the ticket.

ticket_type.description: The name of the ticket type.

ticket_type_description.description: The description of the ticket type.

ticket_type_emoji.description: The emoji of the ticket type.

ticket_custom_state_admin_label.description: The label of the ticket's state as teammates see it.

ticket_custom_state_user_label.description: The label of the ticket's state as the customer sees it.

external_references.description: References linking this conversation to records in an external helpdesk or CRM system. Populated for Fin Standalone workspaces synced from an external platform; an empty array otherwise. Sorted alphabetically by `type` and capped at 20 entries.

monitor_evaluations.description: The latest QA monitor evaluation for each monitor that has evaluated this conversation, whatever its result. Only included when `include_monitors=true` is passed as a query parameter.

scorecards.description: QA scorecard results for this conversation. Only included when `include_scorecards=true` is passed as a query parameter.

conversation.description: Conversations are how you can communicate with users in Intercom. They are created when a contact replies to an outbound message, or when one admin directly sends a message to a single contact.

id.description: The id representing the conversation.

title.description: The title given to the conversation.

created_at.description: The time the conversation was created.

updated_at.description: The last time the conversation was updated.

waiting_since.description: The last time a Contact responded to an Admin. In other words, the time a customer started waiting for a response. Set to null if last reply is from an Admin.

snoozed_until.description: If set this is the time in the future when this conversation will be marked as open. i.e. it will be in a snoozed state until this time. i.e. it will be in a snoozed state until this time.

open.description: Indicates whether a conversation is open (true) or closed (false).

state.description: Can be set to "open", "closed" or "snoozed".

read.description: Indicates whether a conversation has been read.

priority.description: The priority level of the conversation. Returns one of none, low, medium, high, or urgent.

admin_assignee_id.description: The id of the admin assigned to the conversation. If it's not assigned to an admin it will return 0.

team_assignee_id.description: The id of the team assigned to the conversation. If it's not assigned to a team it will return 0.

company.description: The company associated with the conversation.

ai_agent_participated.description: Indicates whether the AI Agent participated in the conversation.

sales_agent_participated.description: Indicates whether the Sales Agent participated in the conversation.

channel.description: The channel through which the conversation was initiated and its current channel.

external_references.description: References linking this conversation to records in an external helpdesk or CRM system. Populated for Fin Standalone workspaces synced from an external platform; an empty array otherwise. Sorted alphabetically by `type` and capped at 20 entries.

monitor_evaluations.description: The latest QA monitor evaluation for each monitor that has evaluated this conversation, whatever its result. Only included when `include_monitors=true` is passed as a query parameter.

scorecards.description: QA scorecard results for this conversation. Only included when `include_scorecards=true` is passed as a query parameter.

conversation_attachment_files.title: Conversation attachment files
conversation_attachment_files.description: Properties of the attachment files in a conversation part

content_type.description: The content type of the file

data.description: The base64 encoded file data.

conversation_channel.title: Conversation Channel
conversation_channel.description: The channel through which a conversation was originally initiated and its current channel.

initial.description: The channel through which the conversation was originally initiated. Possible values include `messenger`, `zendesk_sunshine`, `zendesk_ticket`, `twitter`, `email`. Returns `null` if channel data is unavailable.

current.description: The current channel of the conversation. May differ from `initial` if the conversation was migrated between channels. Returns `null` if channel data is unavailable.

conversation_external_reference.title: Conversation External Reference
conversation_external_reference.description: A reference linking a conversation to a record in an external helpdesk or CRM system, surfaced for Fin Standalone workspaces.

type.description: The type of external system the reference points to. Possible values include `zendesk_ticket`, `zendesk_sunshine_conversation`, `salesforce_case`, `salesforce_in_app_message_conversation`, `freshdesk_ticket`, `freshchat_conversation`, `hubspot_conversation`, `custom_helpdesk_conversation`, `api_conversation`.

id.description: The identifier of the record in the external system. Always serialized as a string, since some external IDs exceed 32-bit integer range.

conversation_monitor_evaluation.title: Conversation Monitor Evaluation
conversation_monitor_evaluation.description: A QA monitor evaluation of this conversation. Returned in the `monitor_evaluations` array on conversation responses when `include_monitors=true` is passed.

monitor_id.description: The unique identifier of the monitor that produced this evaluation.

monitor_name.description: The name of the monitor at the time of evaluation. Null if the monitor has since been deleted.

monitor_type.description: The type of the monitor. Null if the monitor has since been deleted.

result.description: The evaluation outcome reported by the monitor: `included` (the conversation matches the monitor's criteria), `excluded`, `error` or `awaiting_async_data`.

explanation.description: The reasoning provided by the monitor for its result. May be null if no reasoning was generated.

evaluated_at.description: The time the monitor evaluated this conversation. Null in the rare case the underlying record's timestamp is not yet set.

conversation_scorecard.title: Conversation Scorecard
conversation_scorecard.description: A QA scorecard result for this conversation. Returned in the `scorecards` array on conversation responses when `include_scorecards=true` is passed.

scorecard_id.description: The unique identifier of the scorecard definition.

passed.description: Whether the conversation passed the scorecard. Null when the scorecard has not been scored.

score.description: The numeric score for the scorecard. Null when the scorecard has not been scored.

ai_score.description: The numeric score produced by AI evaluation, if applicable. Null when not AI-scored.

evaluated_at.description: The time the scorecard was last evaluated. Null in the rare case the underlying record's timestamp is not yet set.

review_status.description: The status of the review of this scorecard, as shown in the QA reviews list in Intercom. `unreviewed` while the review is waiting for a reviewer's verdict; `submitted` once the review has been submitted; `passed_review`, `needs_fix`, `wont_fix` or `fix_complete` when a teammate set a specific outcome. Null when no review exists for this scorecard.

notes.description: The notes teammates left on the QA review linked to this scorecard entry. Empty when the scorecard has no linked review.

conversation_scorecard_reviewer.title: Reviewer
conversation_scorecard_reviewer.description: Who the review of this scorecard is assigned to. `ai` when it is assigned to Fin; `admin` when it is assigned to a teammate. Null when no review exists for this scorecard or the review is unassigned.

type.description: The kind of reviewer. `ai` if the review is assigned to Fin; `admin` if it is assigned to a teammate.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin the review is assigned to. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_submitted_by.title: Submitted By
conversation_scorecard_submitted_by.description: Who last submitted the review of this scorecard, which can differ from the `reviewer` it is assigned to. `ai` when Fin submitted it; `admin` when a teammate did. Null while the review is unreviewed or when no review exists for this scorecard.

type.description: The kind of submitter. `ai` if Fin submitted the review; `admin` if a teammate did.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who submitted the review. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_revised_by.title: Revised By
conversation_scorecard_revised_by.description: Who last changed the review of this scorecard after it was submitted. `ai` when Fin made the change; `admin` when a teammate did. Null while the review is unreviewed, when it has not been changed since it was submitted, or when no review exists for this scorecard.

type.description: The kind of reviser. `ai` if Fin changed the review; `admin` if a teammate did.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who last changed the review. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_note.title: Scorecard Note
conversation_scorecard_note.description: A note a teammate left on the QA review of this scorecard.

id.description: The id of the note.

created_at.description: The time the note was created.

updated_at.description: The time the note was last edited. Equal to `created_at` when the note has never been edited.

body.description: The text of the note exactly as the teammate entered it. Plain text; it is not rendered as HTML.

conversation_scorecard_note_author.title: Note Author
conversation_scorecard_note_author.description: Who wrote the note. Null when the teammate who wrote it has since been deleted.

type.description: The kind of author. `admin` when a teammate wrote the note; `ai` when Fin did.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who wrote the note. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_reviewed_teammate.title: Reviewed Teammate
conversation_scorecard_reviewed_teammate.description: The teammate (or AI agent) whose handling of the conversation was reviewed by this scorecard.

type.description: The kind of reviewee. `ai` if the conversation was handled by Fin or scored without a specific teammate; `admin` if a specific teammate was reviewed.

admin_id.description: The id of the admin who was reviewed. Present only when `type` is `admin`.

conversation_scorecard_evaluator.title: Conversation Scorecard Evaluator
conversation_scorecard_evaluator.description: A single evaluator within a scorecard, including its result for this conversation.

evaluator_id.description: The unique identifier of the evaluator (criterion) within the scorecard.

name.description: The name of the evaluator (criterion). Null if the evaluator's name could not be resolved.

result.description: The evaluator's result for this conversation. Null if the evaluator was not scored.

conversation_scorecard_evaluator_result.title: Conversation Scorecard Evaluator Result
conversation_scorecard_evaluator_result.description: The outcome of a single evaluator within a scorecard.

value.description: The evaluator's selected value (typically a label such as `pass`, `fail`, or a category identifier).

value_label.description: The label of the rating option matching `value` (for example `Needs improvement`). Omitted when the label could not be resolved.

source.description: The origin of the result (for example, `ai` or `human`).

reasoning.description: A free-text explanation of the result.

reasons.description: The structured reasons chosen for this result. Omitted when none were chosen.

other_text.description: Free-text entered by the reviewer to supplement or stand in for the structured `reasons` — typically captured when the reviewer selects an "Other" option or adds a custom note. Null when not provided.

conversation_scorecard_evaluator_reason.title: Evaluator Reason
conversation_scorecard_evaluator_reason.description: A single structured reason assigned to an evaluator's result.

name.description: The name of the reason. Null if the reason's name could not be resolved.

conversation_contacts.title: Contacts
conversation_contacts.description: The list of contacts (users or leads) involved in this conversation. This will only contain one customer unless more were added via the group conversation feature.

contacts.description: The list of contacts (users or leads) involved in this conversation. This will only contain one customer unless more were added via the group conversation feature.

id.description: The unique identifier for the conversation.

object.description: `conversation`, or `ticket` when the deleted item is a ticket.

deleted.description: Whether the conversation is deleted or not.

deleted_conversation_item.title: Conversation
deleted_conversation_item.description: A deleted conversation record containing its ID, metrics retained status and deletion timestamp.

type.description: String representing the object's type. Always has the value `conversation`.

id.description: The ID of the deleted conversation.

metrics_retained.description: Whether reporting metrics are retained for this conversation ID

deleted_at.description: The time when the conversation was deleted.

external_id.description: The external ID of the contact to issue a token for.

conversation_stream_token.title: Conversation stream token
conversation_stream_token.description: A token that lets a contact's client subscribe to a realtime stream of their conversation events.

type.description: String representing the object's type. Always has the value `conversation_stream_token`.

expires_at.description: The time the token expires, as a UNIX timestamp.

stream.description: What the client needs to connect to the stream.

provider.description: The realtime provider that delivers the stream.

url.description: The host to connect to.

links.description: The requests you can make with this token.

self.description: The request that issues a new token for the contact.

revoke.description: The request that revokes every active token for the contact.

deleted_conversation_list.title: Conversations
deleted_conversation_list.description: A paginated list of deleted conversation IDs.

type.description: String representing the object's type. Always has the value `conversations.list`.

conversations.description: The list of deleted conversation IDs.

total_count.description: Total number of items available.

conversation_first_contact_reply.title: First contact reply
conversation_first_contact_reply.description: An object containing information on the first users message. For a contact initiated message this will represent the users original message.

conversation_list.title: Conversation List
conversation_list.description: Conversations are how you can communicate with users in Intercom. They are created when a contact replies to an outbound message, or when one admin directly sends a message to a single contact.

total_count.description: A count of the total number of objects.

conversation_part.title: Conversation Part
conversation_part.description: A Conversation Part represents a message in the conversation.

id.description: The id representing the conversation part.

part_type.description: The type of conversation part. A part type this version does not recognise is returned as `unknown`; versions before 2.18 return `comment` for those parts. Every value other than `unknown` is also accepted by the `include_part_types` and `exclude_part_types` query parameters when retrieving a conversation.

body.description: The message body, which may contain HTML. For Twitter, this will show a generic message regarding why the body is obscured. In webhook payloads for API version 2.15+, this field returns plain text.

created_at.description: The time the conversation part was created.

updated_at.description: The last time the conversation part was updated.

notified_at.description: The time the user was notified with the conversation part.

user_ip.description: The IP address of the end user who authored this conversation part, when available. Null otherwise, including for parts not authored by an end user.

assigned_to.description: The assignee this conversation_part assigned the conversation to, as a reference whose `type` is `admin`, `team` or `bot`. When the part unassigned the conversation, `type` is `nobody_admin` and `id` is `null`. Null when the part did not change the assignment, or when the assignee has since been deleted.

admin_assignee_id.description: The id of the teammate that this conversation_part assigned the conversation to, or 0 if the part removed the teammate. Null or absent when the part did not change the teammate, including an unassignment that did not name which assignee it cleared. A bot is reported here, because assignment treats anything that is not a team as a teammate.

team_assignee_id.description: The id of the team that this conversation_part assigned the conversation to, or 0 if the part removed the team. Null or absent when the part did not change the team, including an unassignment that did not name which assignee it cleared. A part can assign a team and a teammate at the same time, for example when the team uses Round Robin distribution and the teammate is resolved inline. In that case assigned_to reports only the teammate, and these two fields report each assignee separately.

attachments.title: Conversation part attachments
attachments.description: A list of attachments for the part.

external_id.description: The external id of the conversation part

redacted.description: Whether or not the conversation part has been redacted.

receipts.description: What happened to this part for each recipient it was sent to. Null when delivery receipts have not been recorded for this part.

overall_state.description: The state of the part across all recipients. The worst recipient state wins, except `partially_sent`, which means some recipients have it and others do not.

recipients.description: One entry per recipient the part was sent to, in send order.

participant_id.description: The id of the recipient, a contact id or an admin id.

participant_type.description: Whether the recipient is a contact (`user`) or a teammate (`admin`).

state.description: The delivery state for this recipient.

channel.description: The channel the part was sent on.

state_updated_at.description: The time the state last changed, as a UTC Unix timestamp.

error_code.description: The reason Intercom could not send to this recipient, when it could not. Null otherwise.

address.description: The email address the part was sent to, for contact recipients. Null for teammates or when it is not known.

state.description: Indicates the current state of conversation when the conversation part was created.

tags.description: A list of tags objects associated with the conversation part.

app_package_code.description: The app package code if this part was created via API. null if the part was not created via API.

translations.description: A map of the reply text keyed by locale code. Backs the `conversation.admin.replied.translated` webhook topic. `original` holds the locale code the reply was written in, when it is known; every other key holds the reply translated into that locale.

original.description: The locale code identifying the language the reply was originally written in.

conversation_part_author.title: Conversation part author
conversation_part_author.description: The object who initiated the conversation, which can be a Contact, Admin or Team. Bots and campaigns send messages on behalf of Admins or Teams. For Twitter, this will be blank.

id.description: The id of the author

name.description: The name of the author. `null` if the author is a contact that has since been archived or deleted.

email.description: The email of the author. `null` if the author is a contact that has since been archived or deleted.

from_ai_agent.description: If this conversation part was sent by the AI Agent

is_ai_answer.description: If this conversation part body was generated by the AI Agent

conversation_parts.title: Conversation Parts
conversation_parts.description: A list of Conversation Part objects for each part message in the conversation. This is only returned when Retrieving a Conversation, and ignored when Listing all Conversations. There is a limit of 500 parts.

conversation_parts.title: Conversation Parts
conversation_parts.description: A list of Conversation Part objects for each part message in the conversation. This is only returned when Retrieving a Conversation, and ignored when Listing all Conversations. There is a limit of 500 parts.

total_count.description: A count of the conversation parts in this response, after any `include_part_types` or `exclude_part_types` filter has been applied. When paginating, this is the number of parts on the current page. This is not the conversation's total part count.

pages.description: Pagination details for the conversation parts. Only returned when the `page` query parameter is sent. `next` is null on the last page.

quick_reply_options.description: The quick reply options sent by the Admin or bot, presented in this conversation part.

translations.description: The translations for the quick reply option.

quick_reply_option_uuid.description: The unique identifier for the quick reply option that was clicked by the end user.

conversation_rating.title: Conversation Rating
conversation_rating.description: The Conversation Rating object which contains information on the rating and/or remark added by a Contact and the Admin assigned to the conversation.

rating.description: The rating, between 1 and 5, for the conversation.

remark.description: An optional field to add a remark to correspond to the number rating

created_at.description: The time the rating was requested in the conversation being rated.

updated_at.description: The time the rating was last updated.

teammate.title: Conversation Rating Teammate
teammate.description: The teammate, bot or workflow the rating is attributed to.

type.description: The type of the rated actor. `workflow` when a workflow requested the rating and no teammate took part.

id.description: The unique identifier for the rated actor.

conversation_response_time.title: Conversation response time
conversation_response_time.description: Details of first response time of assigned team in seconds.

team_name.description: Name of the assigned Team, null if team does not exist, Unassigned if no team is assigned.

response_time.description: First response time of assigned team in seconds.

intercom_user_id.description: The unique identifier for the contact the rating request was sent to.

remark.description: Free text from the contact to go with the rating.

rated_conversation.title: Rated conversation
rated_conversation.description: The CSAT rating recorded on a conversation.

type.description: String representing the object's type. Always has the value `conversation_rating`.

conversation_id.description: The unique identifier for the conversation.

remark.description: The free text left with the rating.

created_at.description: The time the rating request was created, as a UNIX timestamp.

updated_at.description: The time the rating or remark last changed, as a UNIX timestamp.

id.description: The unique identifier for the contact.

type.description: `admin` for a teammate, `bot` for Fin, or `workflow` for a workflow.

id.description: The unique identifier for the teammate, Fin or workflow. For a deleted workflow, this is the identifier recorded with the rating.

conversation_source.title: Conversation source
conversation_source.description: The type of the conversation part that started this conversation. Can be Contact, Admin, Campaign, Automated or Operator initiated.

id.description: The id of the source message.

user_ip.description: The IP address of the end user who opened this conversation, when available. Null otherwise, including when the conversation was not opened by an end user.

recipients.description: The recipients of the source message. Only present for email conversations.

type.description: The recipient type. One of `to`, `cc`, or `bcc`.

email.description: The recipient email address.

drop_reason.description: The reason this recipient was dropped, if applicable.

reply_to.description: The Reply-To header addresses of the source message, where a reply will be routed. Can differ from the sender's From address. Only present for email conversations.

email.description: The Reply-To email address.

name.description: The display name associated with the Reply-To address.

subject.description: Optional. The message subject. For Twitter, this will show a generic message regarding why the subject is obscured. In webhook payloads for API version 2.15+, this field returns plain text.

body.description: The message body, which may contain HTML. For Twitter, this will show a generic message regarding why the body is obscured. In webhook payloads for API version 2.15+, this field returns plain text.

attachments.description: A list of attachments for the part.

url.description: The URL where the conversation was started. For Twitter, Email, and Bots, this will be blank.

redacted.description: Whether or not the source message has been redacted. Only applicable for contact initiated messages.

conversation_source_author.title: Conversation source author
conversation_source_author.description: The author who started the conversation. Can be a Contact, Admin, or Bot.

id.description: The id of the author.

email.description: The email of the author.

source_email_message_metadata.title: Email Message Metadata
source_email_message_metadata.description: Contains metadata if the message was sent as an email

message_id.description: The unique identifier for the email message as specified in the Message-ID header

email_address_headers.title: Email Address Headers
email_address_headers.description: A list of an email address headers.

history.description: The HTML content of any quoted or forwarded email history from the initial inbound message

conversation_statistics.title: Conversation statistics
conversation_statistics.description: A Statistics object containing all information required for reporting, with timestamps and calculated metrics.

time_to_assignment.description: Duration until last assignment before first admin reply. In seconds.

time_to_admin_reply.description: Duration until first admin reply. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.

time_to_first_close.description: Duration until conversation was closed first time. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.

time_to_last_close.description: Duration until conversation was closed last time. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.

median_time_to_reply.description: Median based on all admin replies after a contact reply. Subtracts out of business hours. In seconds.

first_contact_reply_at.description: Time of first text conversation part from a contact.

first_assignment_at.description: Time of first assignment after first_contact_reply_at.

first_admin_reply_at.description: Time of first admin reply after first_contact_reply_at.

first_close_at.description: Time of first close after first_contact_reply_at.

last_assignment_at.description: Time of last assignment after first_contact_reply_at.

last_assignment_admin_reply_at.description: Time of first admin reply since most recent assignment.

last_contact_reply_at.description: Time of the last conversation part from a contact.

last_admin_reply_at.description: Time of the last conversation part from an admin.

last_close_at.description: Time of the last conversation close.

last_closed_by_id.description: The last admin who closed the conversation. Returns a reference to an Admin object.

assigned_team_first_response_time.description: An array of conversation response time objects

assigned_team_first_response_time_in_off.description: An array of conversation response time objects within office hours

handling_time.description: Time from conversation assignment to conversation close in seconds.

adjusted_handling_time.description: Adjusted handling time for conversation in seconds. This is the active handling time excluding idle periods when teammates are not actively working on the conversation.

conversation_teammates.title: Conversation teammates
conversation_teammates.description: The list of teammates who participated in the conversation (wrote at least one conversation part).

admins.description: The list of teammates who participated in the conversation (wrote at least one conversation part).

convert_conversation_to_ticket_request.description: You can convert a Conversation to a Ticket
convert_conversation_to_ticket_request.title: Convert Ticket Request Payload

ticket_type_id.description: The ID of the type of ticket you want to convert the conversation to

ticket_state_id.description: The ID of the ticket state associated with the ticket type.

convert_visitor_request.description: You can merge a Visitor to a Contact of role type lead or user.
convert_visitor_request.title: Convert Visitor Request Payload

type.description: Represents the role of the Contact model. Accepts `lead` or `user`.

user.description: The unique identifiers retained after converting or merging. Required when `type` is `user`; not read when `type` is `lead`.

id.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.

user_id.description: A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom, which will be represented as external_id.

email.description: The contact's email, retained by default if one is present.

visitor.description: The unique identifiers to convert a single Visitor. One of `id` or `user_id` is required; an `email` on its own does not identify a visitor.

id.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.

user_id.description: A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom.

email.description: The visitor's email.

create_audience_request.title: Create Audience Request
create_audience_request.description: The request payload for creating an audience.

predicates.description: The predicates that define which contacts belong to the audience.

role_predicates.description: Role-based predicates that further filter audience membership by contact role. Defaults to all three contact roles when omitted.

title.description: The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content. Required unless a title is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.

description.description: The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.

body.description:
The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`. Empty `

` tags are kept as blank paragraphs instead of being dropped.

body_markdown.description: The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

author_id.description: The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace. Required unless an `author_id` is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.

state.description: Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Defaults to draft. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.

parent_id.description: The id of the article's parent collection or section. An article without this field stands alone.

parent_ids.description: The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to leave the article without a collection. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.

locale.description: The locale of the article's default content, for example `en`. Defaults to the locale of the help center that the parent collection belongs to when `parent_id` is sent, and otherwise to the default Help Center locale. Must be a locale supported by the workspace's Help Center.

translated_content.description: Content for other locales, keyed by locale code. Content for the article's default locale can also be given here instead of at the top level. If it is given in both places, the values must match.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to leave it without a folder.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.

ai_chatbot_availability.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

scheduled_publish_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

scheduled_unpublish_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The same request must also publish the article (`state: "published"`), otherwise it returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

create_internal_article_request.description: You can create an Internal Article
create_internal_article_request.title: Create Internal Article Request Payload

title.description: The title of the article.

body.description: The content of the article in HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.

body_markdown.description: The content of the article in markdown. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `json_blocks`.

json_blocks.description: The content of the article as a list of content blocks. Used only when `body` is not provided. Cannot be combined with `body_markdown`.

locale.description: The locale of the article. Defaults to `en`.

author_id.description: The id of the author of the article.

owner_id.description: The id of the owner of the article.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder to place this article in. Pass `null` to leave it without a folder.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to target this internal article to for Fin AI Agent. Pass an empty array or omit the field for no audience targeting. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.

ai_chatbot_availability.description: Whether the internal article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). Defaults to false.

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the internal article should be available for AI Copilot. Defaults to false.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the internal article should be available for AI Sales Agent. Defaults to false.

name.description: The name of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the name of the default language's content. Required unless a name is provided in `translated_content` under the workspace's default Help Center locale.

description.description: The description of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the description of the default language's content.

icon.description: The icon of the collection, for example `book-bookmark`. Defaults to `book-bookmark`.

parent_id.description: The id of the parent collection. If `null` then it will be created as the first level collection.

help_center_id.description: The id of the help center where the collection will be created. If `null` then it will be created in the default help center.

role.description: The role of the contact. `lead` creates a lead; any other value creates a user.

external_id.description: A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom

email_verified.description:
Whether the contact has proved they own this email address, for example through a confirmation link or one-time code you sent. Send it together with `email`. `email_verified` without `email` is rejected.

Changing a contact's email resets it to not verified. Intercom reuses leads with a verified email when an inbound email, conversation or ticket matches the address.

email.description: The contacts email

avatar.description: An image URL containing the avatar of a contact

signed_up_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.

last_seen_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).

owner_id.description: The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact

unsubscribed_from_emails.description: Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails

sms_consent.description: Whether the contact has consented to receive SMS messages.

unsubscribed_from_sms.description: Whether the contact is unsubscribed from SMS messages.

language_override.description: A preferred language setting for the contact, used by the Intercom Messenger even if their browser settings change.

custom_attributes.description: The custom attributes which are set for the contact

create_content_import_source_request.title: Create Content Import Source Payload
create_content_import_source_request.description: You can add an Content Import Source to your Fin Content Library.

sync_behavior.description: If you intend to create or update External Pages via the API, this should be set to `api`.

status.description: The status of the content import source.

url.description: The URL of the content import source. It must be an http or https URL whose host is a valid public domain name.

audience_ids.description: The unique identifiers for the audiences to associate with this content import source. Can be a single integer or an array of integers.

create_conversation_request.description: Conversations are how you can communicate with users in Intercom. They are created when a contact replies to an outbound message, or when one admin directly sends a message to a single contact.
create_conversation_request.title: Create Conversation Request Payload

type.description: The role associated to the contact - user or lead.

id.description: The identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom. Provide one of `id`, `user_id` or `email`. If you send more than one, `id` is used first, then `user_id`.

user_id.description: The external identifier you gave the user. Matches users only; for a lead, use `id` or `email`.

email.description: The contact's email. Matches a user or a lead, depending on `type`. Used only when `user_id` isn't sent. If several leads share the email and it's the only identifier sent, the request fails with `multiple_users`; use `id` instead.

body.description: The content of the message. HTML is not supported.

subject.description: The title of the email. Only applicable if the message type is email.

attachment_urls.description: A list of image URLs that will be added as attachments. You can include up to 10 URLs.

created_at.description: The time the conversation was created as a UTC Unix timestamp. If not provided, the current time will be used. This field is only recommneded for migrating past conversations from another source into Intercom.

brand_id.description: The unique identifier of the brand to associate with this conversation.

name.description: The name of the data attribute.

model.description: The model that the data attribute belongs to.

description.description: The readable description you see in the UI for the attribute.

messenger_writable.description: Can this attribute be updated by the Messenger

options.description: Array of objects representing the options of the list, with `value` as the key and the option as the value. At least two options are required.

event_name.description: The name of the event that occurred. This is presented to your App's admins when filtering and creating segments - a good event name is typically a past tense 'verb-noun' combination, to improve readability, for example `updated-plan`.

created_at.description: The time the event occurred as a UTC Unix timestamp

user_id.description: Your identifier for the user.

id.description: The unique identifier for the contact (lead or user) which is given by Intercom.

email.description: An email address for your user. An email should only be used where your application uses email to uniquely identify users.

metadata.description: Optional metadata about the event. Values can be a string, a number, a boolean, or an object holding a rich link (`url` and `value`) or a monetary amount (`amount` and `currency`).

create_data_event_summaries_request.description: You can send a list of event summaries for a user. Each event summary should contain the event name, the time the event occurred, and the number of times the event occurred. The event name should be a past tense "verb-noun" combination, to improve readability, for example `updated-plan`.
create_data_event_summaries_request.title: Create Data Event Summaries Request

user_id.description: Your identifier for the user.

id.description: The Intercom defined id of the user. Takes precedence over `user_id` and `email`.

email.description: The user's email address. Only used when neither `id` nor `user_id` is supplied.

event_summaries.description: A list of event summaries for the user. Each event summary should contain the event name, the time the event occurred, and the number of times the event occurred. The event name should be a past tense 'verb-noun' combination, to improve readability, for example `updated-plan`.

event_name.description: The name of the event that occurred. A good event name is typically a past tense 'verb-noun' combination, to improve readability, for example `updated-plan`.

count.description: The number of times the event occurred.

first.description: The first time the event was sent

last.description: The last time the event was sent

create_data_exports_request.description: Request for creating a data export
create_data_exports_request.title: Create Data Export Request

created_at_after.description: The start date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a unix timestamp.

created_at_before.description: The end date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a unix timestamp.

create_external_page_request.title: Create External Page Payload
create_external_page_request.description: You can add an External Page to your Fin Content Library.

title.description: The title of the external page.

html.description: The body of the external page in HTML.

url.description: The URL of the external page. This will be used by Fin to link end users to the page it based its answer on. When a URL is not present, Fin will not reference the source.

ai_agent_availability.description: Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Agent. Will not default when updating an existing external page.

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Copilot. Will not default when updating an existing external page.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Sales Agent. Will not default when updating an existing external page.

locale.description: The language code of the external page, for example `en` or `fr`. It must be a language supported by the workspace.

source_id.description: The unique identifier for the source of the external page which was given by Intercom. Every external page must be associated with a Content Import Source which represents the place it comes from and from which it inherits a default audience (configured in the UI). For a new source, make a POST request to the Content Import Source endpoint and an ID for the source will be returned in the response.

external_id.description: The identifier for the external page which was given by the source. Must be unique for the source.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to target this external page to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field keeps the default audience inherited from the source. Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships, including the inherited ones. If an external page already exists with the specified source_id and external_id, omitting the field leaves its audience memberships unchanged. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error.

message_type.description: The kind of message being created. Values: `in_app`, `email` or `whatsapp`. `inapp` is also accepted for in-app messages, and responses always show in-app messages as `inapp`.

body.description: The content of the message. HTML and plaintext are supported.

template.description: For `email` messages, the style of the outgoing message. Possible values `plain` or `personal`. For `whatsapp` messages, the name of the WhatsApp message template to send. A template that doesn't exist returns a `400` error.

from.description: The sender of the message. Required. A request without `from` returns a `400` error.

id.description: The identifier for the admin which is given by Intercom.

oneOf.title: WhatsApp recipient

name.description: The name to give the contact if one is created.

oneOf.description: The CC recipients of the message.

created_at.description: The time the message was created. If not provided, the current time will be used.

create_conversation_without_contact_repl.description: Whether a conversation should be opened in the inbox for the message without the contact replying. Defaults to false if not provided. For `whatsapp` messages, a conversation is always opened and this field is ignored.

components.description: The components of the WhatsApp template, with the values for its variables. Required for `whatsapp` messages.

locale.description: The locale of the WhatsApp template to send, such as `en`. If you leave it out, the contact's messenger locale is used, then the workspace locale. A template that isn't available in the locale returns a `400` error.

type.description: The role associated to the contact - `user` or `lead`.

id.description: The identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom.

create_or_update_company_request.title: Create Or Update Company Request Payload
create_or_update_company_request.description: You can create or update a Company. Send either `company_id` or `id`; a request with neither returns a `400` error.

company_id.description: The company id you have defined for the company. Can't be updated

size.description: The number of employees in this company.

industry.description: The industry that this company operates in.

monthly_spend.description: How much revenue the company generates for your business. Floats are truncated to whole integers, so 155.98 is stored as 155. A value above 2147483647 (2**31-1) is stored as 0. 2147483647 itself, or a value of -2147483648 or below, returns a `422` error.

create_or_update_custom_object_instance_.description: Payload to create or update a Custom Object instance
create_or_update_custom_object_instance_.title: Create Or Update Custom Object Instance Request Payload

external_id.description: A unique identifier for the Custom Object instance in the external system it originated from. The value `reference_not_found` is reserved and is rejected with a `400`. Omitting this field creates a new instance on every request instead of updating an existing one.

external_created_at.description: The time when the Custom Object instance was created in the external system it originated from. A value that cannot be read as a time is stored as `null` rather than rejected.

external_updated_at.description: The time when the Custom Object instance was last updated in the external system it originated from. A value that cannot be read as a time is stored as `null` rather than rejected.

custom_attributes.description:
The custom attributes which are set for the Custom Object instance.

Each value must match the type of the attribute it is set on: a string, integer, number or boolean, a Unix timestamp or date string for a datetime attribute, or `null` to clear the attribute. A list attribute takes the label or id of one of its options; a value that matches no option clears the attribute rather than being rejected. A reference attribute takes the Intercom id of the record it points at, or an array of ids for a reference to several records; an id that matches no record is skipped.

create_or_update_tag_request.description: You can create or update an existing tag, and optionally apply it to a list of contact or company ids.
create_or_update_tag_request.title: Create or Update Tag Request Payload

name.description: The name of the tag, which will be created if not found, or the new name for the tag if this is an update request. Names are case insensitive and can be at most 191 characters long. Creating a tag with a longer name returns a 400. When updating by `id`, a longer name or one that another tag already has returns 200 with the new name, but the tag keeps its old name.

ids_to_add.description: The Intercom ids of the contacts or companies to apply the tag to. A contact id that does not exist returns a 404; a company id that does not exist is skipped. conversation_to_link_id.description:

 - conversation | tracker ticket
 - customer ticket | tracker ticket

created_at.description: The time the ticket was created. If not provided, the current time will be used.

admin_assignee_id.description: The ID of the admin to which the ticket is assigned. If not provided, the ticket will be unassigned.

team_assignee_id.description: The ID of the team to which the ticket is assigned. If not provided, the ticket will be unassigned.

channel.description: The channel for the ticket. Only supported for customer ticket types. Defaults to messenger if not provided.

name.description: The name of the ticket type attribute

cursor_pages.title: Cursor based pages
cursor_pages.description:
Cursor-based pagination is a technique used in the Intercom API to navigate through large amounts of data.
A "cursor" or pointer is used to keep track of the current position in the result set, allowing the API to return the data in small chunks or "pages" as needed.

next.description: Fetch the next page by sending this `starting_after` cursor. Omitted on the last page.

page.description: The number of the next page

call.title: Call

data_export.title: Data Export
data_export.description: The data export API is used to export message delivery and engagement statistics for outbound content (Emails, Posts, Custom Bots, Surveys, Tours, Series, and more) sent in a given timeframe. The exported data includes who received each message, when they received it, and how they engaged with it (opens, clicks, replies, completions, dismissals, unsubscribes, and bounces).

status.description: The current state of your job.

download_expires_at.description: The time after which you will not be able to access the data, as a Unix timestamp. It is one week from the time the job was created. Empty until the job completes.

download_url.description: The location where you can download your data. Empty until the job completes.

user_id.description: The user_id of the user who was sent the message.

user_external_id.description: The external_user_id of the user who was sent the message

company_id.description: The company ID of the user in relation to the message that was sent. Will return -1 if no company is present.

email.description: The users email who was sent the message.

name.description: The full name of the user receiving the message

content_id.description: The specific content that was received. In an A/B test each version has its own Content ID.

content_title.description: The title of the content you see in your Intercom workspace.

ruleset_version_id.description: As you edit content we record new versions. This ID can help you determine which version of a piece of content that was received.

receipt_id.description: ID for this receipt. Will be included with any related stats in other files to identify this specific delivery of a message.

received_at.description: Timestamp for when the receipt was recorded.

series_id.description: The id of the series that this content is part of. Will return -1 if not part of a series.

series_title.description: The title of the series that this content is part of.

node_id.description: The id of the series node that this ruleset is associated with. Each block in a series has a corresponding node_id.

first_reply.description: The first time a user replied to this message if the content was able to receive replies. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_completion.description: The first time a user completed this message if the content was able to be completed e.g. Tours, Surveys. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_series_completion.description: The first time the series this message was a part of was completed by the user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_series_disengagement.description: The first time the series this message was a part of was disengaged by the user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_series_exit.description: The first time the series this message was a part of was exited by the user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_goal_success.description: The first time the user met this messages associated goal if one exists. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_open.description: The first time the user opened this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_click.description: The first time the series the user clicked on a link within this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_dismisall.description: The first time the series the user dismissed this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_unsubscribe.description: The first time the user unsubscribed from this message. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

first_hard_bounce.description: The first time this message hard bounced for this user. Only events within the export job's requested date range are counted.

ecommerce_catalog_variant.title: Ecommerce Catalog Variant
ecommerce_catalog_variant.description: A product variant in an ecommerce catalog upload.

id.description: Unique identifier for this variant within the product.

title.description: Variant display name shown to shoppers (e.g. "Small / Blue").

price.description: Price of this specific variant. Fin uses variant prices for precise budget filtering and displays the variant price in recommendation cards.

compare_at_price.description: Original price before a discount. When provided, Fin will naturally mention the saving to the shopper (e.g. "down from $129 to $99").

in_stock.description: Whether this variant is currently available. Out-of-stock variants are not shown in Fin's recommendation cards and Fin will not suggest them to shoppers.

url.description: Direct link to this variant's page. Takes precedence over the product URL in recommendation cards. If omitted, constructed automatically as `{product_url}?variant={id}`.

image_url.description: Image specific to this variant. Takes precedence over the product's `featured_image_url`. Falls back to `featured_image_url`, then `image_urls`. If no valid image can be resolved, this variant's recommendation card will not be shown.

selected_options.description: The specific option values that define this variant (e.g. Size=Small, Color=Blue). Fin uses these to match shopper requests like "do you have this in medium?" to the correct variant.

sku.description: Stock-keeping unit for this specific variant. Fin uses this to resolve shopper requests like "do you have this in size M?" to the exact variant, and can quote it back when a shopper asks for it directly.

ecommerce_catalog_product.title: Ecommerce Catalog Product
ecommerce_catalog_product.description:
A product object in an ecommerce catalog upload. The catalog file must be a JSON
array of these objects. The `id`, `title`, and `url` fields are required; all
others are optional.

id.description: Your unique product identifier. Used to match products on re-upload so only changed products are re-indexed. Also the delete key — any product ID absent from a new upload is removed from Fin's knowledge. Must be stable across uploads.

title.description: Product name. Used by Fin when searching for and recommending products.

url.description: Canonical product page URL shown in Fin's product recommendations. Must be a valid https:// URL.

description.description: Product description that Fin reads to understand what the product is. HTML formatting is supported and safely sanitized (`description_html` takes precedence if both are provided). This is the primary field Fin uses to match products to shopper questions — a richer description leads to better recommendations.

description_html.description: HTML product description. Takes precedence over `description` when both are provided. HTML is safely sanitized before indexing.

featured_image_url.description: Primary product image shown in Fin's recommendation cards. Falls back to the first entry of `image_urls` if not provided. If no valid image can be resolved for a variant, that variant's recommendation card is not shown to the shopper.

image_urls.description: Additional product images. Used as a fallback image source when `featured_image_url` is absent or when a variant has no specific image.

price_min.description: Lowest price across all variants. If omitted, derived automatically from variant prices. Fin uses this to filter products when a shopper mentions a budget (e.g. "under $100"). Displayed as a range alongside `price_max`, or as a single value if both are equal.

price_max.description: Highest price across all variants. If omitted, derived from variant prices. Used alongside `price_min` for budget filtering and price display.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for all prices on this product (e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP"). Defaults to USD if omitted. Used to format prices with the correct symbol in Fin's responses and product cards.

in_stock.description:
Whether the product is available to purchase. If omitted, derived from variant stock — the
product is in stock if at least one variant has `in_stock: true`. Products with no in-stock
variants are hidden from Fin entirely and will not be recommended to shoppers.

tags.description: Free-form keywords matching how shoppers phrase needs in chat (e.g. "waterproof", "gift", "plus-size"). Used by Fin to match fuzzy queries; complements `category_path` and `collections`.

collections.description: Collections or groupings this product belongs to in your store. Fin uses collections to understand your catalog's structure and answer questions like "what's in the sale collection?". Each element may be a plain string or an object with a `title` field.

category_path.description:
Hierarchical category breadcrumb for the product. Fin understands the hierarchy — a
shopper asking about "Clothing" will see products from all subcategories underneath it.
The most specific category is shown in search results. Strongly recommended. Provide as
a pre-formatted string (e.g. `"Clothing > T-Shirts"`) or as an array of path segments
(e.g. `["Clothing", "T-Shirts"]`). Array segments are joined with ` > `.

available_options.description:
Option types available for this product and their possible values
(e.g. `{"name": "Size", "values": ["S", "M", "L"]}`). Fin uses these to understand what
choices a shopper can make and to correctly filter variants when a shopper asks for a
specific size, colour, or other attribute.

values.description: All available values for this option.

variants.description: Individual purchasable variants of the product. Fin recommends specific variants (not just products), so populating variants with accurate stock, price, and option data leads to more precise recommendations. See `ecommerce_catalog_variant` for the variant object schema.

additional_data.description: Custom attributes for your business. Fin uses these to show each customer only the products relevant to them (e.g. regional availability or warehouse codes). All keys must be consistent across all products in your catalog — the attribute schema is read from the first product in the file.

ecommerce_product_event_product.title: Ecommerce Product Event Product
ecommerce_product_event_product.description:
The full product sent in a `product.created` or `product.updated` event. It uses the same
fields as `ecommerce_catalog_product`, plus `updated_at`, which is required. The serialized
product must be 60 KB or smaller.

created_at.description: When the product was created in your store, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_at.description: When the product was last changed in your store, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

occurred_at.description: When the change happened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

data.description: The event payload. Send `product` for `product.created` and `product.updated`, and `product_id` for `product.deleted`.

product_id.description: The `id` of the product to delete. Required for `product.deleted`.

ecommerce_product_event_response.description: Returned when a product event is accepted and queued.

custom_action_started.description: Contains details about name of the action that was initiated for conversation part type custom_action_started.

custom_action_finished.title: Part type - custom_action_finished
custom_action_finished.description: Contains details about final status of the completed action for conversation part type custom_action_finished.

operator_workflow_event.description: Contains details about name of the workflow for conversation part type operator_workflow_event.

call_summary.description: Contains the id of the call the summary describes, for conversation part type call_summary. A conversation can contain several calls, and therefore several call summaries, so this identifies which call each summary belongs to. The id matches the id returned by the Calls API and by the call.started, call.ended, call.recording_available and call.transcription_available webhook topics.

call_id.description: The id of the call the summary describes

ai_agent_event_otp_email_verification_fa.title: Part type - ai_agent_event (otp_email_verification_failed)
ai_agent_event_otp_email_verification_fa.description: Contains the reason Fin could not verify a contact by one-time passcode email, for conversation part type ai_agent_event when the event type is otp_email_verification_failed. Other ai_agent_event event types are not described here.

value.description: A readable label for the event

data.description: Data recorded with the event. Empty when the failure was recorded without a reason.

reason.description: Why the one-time passcode email could not verify the contact. Treat this as a free-form string and fall back to value for a reason you do not recognise. no_email means the contact has no email address on record.

standalone_platform_handoff.title: Part type - standalone_platform_handoff
standalone_platform_handoff.description: Contains the handoff Fin attempted to an external platform, for conversation part type standalone_platform_handoff.

type.description: The handoff type. One of zendesk_ticket, zendesk_agent, salesforce_case, salesforce_in_app_messaging, salesforce_team, external_agent or external_ticket. Older parts can also return salesforce_chat.

success.description: true when the handoff completed and false when it failed. null means no outcome was recorded on this part, for example a Salesforce in-app messaging handoff that was only initiated.

data.description: Details of the handoff. Always present. For a successful salesforce_case handoff it holds the created Case's case_id and case_number; otherwise it is an empty object.

case_id.description: The ID of the Salesforce Case created by the handoff.

case_number.description: The number of the Salesforce Case created by the handoff.

error.title: Error
error.description: The API will return an Error List for a failed request, which will contain one or more Error objects.

errors.description: An array of one or more error objects

code.description: A string indicating the kind of error, used to further qualify the HTTP response code.

message.description: Optional. Human readable description of the error.

data.description: Optional. Extra detail about the error, for example `required_permissions` on a 403 `action_forbidden` error.

external_page.title: External Page
external_page.description: External pages that you have added to your Fin Content Library.

title.description: The title of the external page.

html.description: The body of the external page in HTML.

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the external page should be used to answer questions by AI Copilot.

locale.description: The language code of the external page, for example `en` or `fr`.

source_id.description: The unique identifier for the source of the external page which was given by Intercom. Every external page must be associated with a Content Import Source which represents the place it comes from and from which it inherits a default audience (configured in the UI). For a new source, make a POST request to the Content Import Source endpoint and an ID for the source will be returned in the response.

external_id.description: The identifier for the external page which was given by the source. Must be unique for the source.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs that this external page is targeted to for Fin AI Agent. Empty when the external page has no audience targeting.

updated_at.description: The time when the external page was last updated.

last_ingested_at.description: The time when the external page was last ingested.

tags.description: The tags applied to the external page.

fin_agent_message.title: Fin Agent Message
fin_agent_message.description: A message exchanged within a Fin Agent conversation.

author.description: The author that created the message. In `conversation_metadata.history`, only `user` and `agent` are accepted.

body.description:
The body of the message. Accepts both plain text and HTML format.
For the message you send to Fin, this is the user's message. For an `agent` item in `conversation_metadata.history`, it is the agent's message.
Fin's response is returned in the format set by `response_format` (HTML by default).

timestamp.description:
The timestamp when the message was created.
Used to deduplicate messages sent within a 5 minute window.
Ideally should include milliseconds for higher precision.
Send `timestamp` or `timestamp_ms`; at least one is required. If you send both, `timestamp_ms` is used.
On the top-level `message`, sending neither fails with a 422 error (`message: timestamp_ms is required`). In `conversation_metadata.history`, an item with neither causes the whole history to be ignored.

timestamp_ms.description:
The timestamp when the message was created, with millisecond precision.
Accepted in place of `timestamp` when you send a message, and also present in webhook event responses (fin_replied). At least one of `timestamp` or `timestamp_ms` is required.

fin_agent_user.title: Fin Agent User
fin_agent_user.description: A user object representing the user in a Fin Agent conversation.

id.description:
The ID of the user. This value will be used to uniquely identify the user

email.description: The email of the user.

attributes.description:
