fin_agent_attachment.description:
An attachment object representing a file or URL attachment included with a message.
Attachments can be used to provide additional context to Fin.
Maximum of 10 attachments per request.

url.description: The URL of the attachment. Required when type is 'url'. Must be publicly accessible.

name.description: The name of the file. Required when type is 'file'.

content_type.description: The MIME type of the file. Required when type is 'file'.

data.description: Base64-encoded file data. Required when type is 'file'.

fin_agent_conversation_metadata.title: Fin Agent Conversation Metadata
fin_agent_conversation_metadata.description: Metadata about the conversation, including history and attributes.

history.description:
An array of previous messages in the conversation before Fin is initialized.
This data provides context to Fin and helps generate a better answer.
Limit to the last 10 messages.
Only `user` and `agent` authors are accepted. If any item is invalid, for example it has no `timestamp` or `timestamp_ms`, or has another author, the whole history is ignored.

attributes.description:
A hash of attributes associated with the conversation.
These attributes can be used by Fin to provide more contextual responses.
Limit to 20 attributes.

fin_agent_attribute_errors.description: Contains error details if any user or conversation attribute updates failed.

Map of conversation attribute names to error messages.

fin_agent_status_updated_event.title: Fin Agent Status Updated Event
fin_agent_status_updated_event.description:
Event fired when Fin's status changes during a conversation.
Delivered via webhooks. Fin will report its status to the client via this event.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation.

user_id.description: The ID of the user.

status.description:
Fin's current status.
- thinking: Fin has started running a procedure. Not sent on every turn
- awaiting_user_reply: Fin has finished replying and is waiting for the user to respond
- escalated: The conversation has been escalated to a human
- resolved: The user's query has been resolved
- complete: Fin has completed its workflow. When CSAT is enabled a csat_requested event may follow

reason.description:
Optional. A human-readable explanation of why the conversation was escalated.
Only present when status is 'escalated'.

When you escalate deterministically with `/fin/escalate`, the reason is always
"Escalation requested via API".

The following reasons apply to Fin-decided escalations when Fin owns the
conversation (`/fin/start`, `/fin/procedures/{procedure_id}/run`, and
`/fin/reply` on a conversation that was started that way). `/fin/ask` can
report any of them, because escalation rules still apply and the conversation
can still be routed to a team or finish without resolution. On an Ask,
"Escalation requested by user" normally only follows an escalation rule match.
- "Escalation requested by user"
- "Escalation rule: {rule_name}"
- "Escalation rule matched"
- "Routed to team"
- "Conversation finished without resolution"

"Escalation requested by user" is sent whenever Fin decides to hand over, not
only when the user asks for a human, for example on a procedure handoff or a
custom answer handover. It also follows an escalation rule match, as a second
`escalated` event after the rule's reason. While a procedure is running, every
escalation Fin decides on reports it.

created_at_ms.description: The timestamp the event was created at, with millisecond precision.

fin_agent_replied_event.title: Fin Agent Replied Event
fin_agent_replied_event.description:
Event fired when Fin replies to a user.
Delivered via webhooks. The content of the response will be contained in the message object.
Intermediate replies have status 'replying'; a separate fin_status_updated event with 'awaiting_user_reply' fires once Fin's reply is done.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation.

user_id.description: The ID of the user.

message.description: Fin's answer to the user's query.

id.description: A unique identifier for this message.

author.description: The author of the message (always 'fin' for this event).

body.description: The body of Fin's response, in the format given by `format` (HTML by default).

format.description: Present only when the request set `response_format` to `markdown`. `markdown` when Fin converted the reply to Markdown, or `html` if it could not convert the reply and sent HTML instead. When absent, `body` is HTML.

timestamp_ms.description: The timestamp the message was created at, with millisecond precision.

sources.description:
The content sources Fin used to generate this reply, in the same order as the
[n] citation markers in the body. Present only when Fin cited content.

title.description: The title of the source.

type.description: Whether the source is an Intercom article or external content.

url.description: The URL of the source.

status.description:
Fin's current status.
- replying: Intermediate reply part; more parts may follow
- awaiting_user_reply: Legacy status; instead use the fin_status_updated event with 'awaiting_user_reply', which fires once Fin's reply is done
- complete: Fin's reply is final and no user reply is expected. Sent for one-shot Ask replies only

created_at_ms.description: The timestamp the event was created at, with millisecond precision.

fin_agent_csat_requested_event.title: Fin Agent CSAT Requested Event
fin_agent_csat_requested_event.description:
Event fired when Fin asks the user to rate the conversation.
Delivered via webhooks. Carries the rating options to present to the user; submit
the user's choice with POST /fin/csat. Unlike the reply events it has no message — a
rating survey is a set of options to choose from, not readable text.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation.

user_id.description: The ID of the user.

csat.description: The rating survey to present to the user.

options.description: The ordered rating options to show the user.

key.description: The stable key to send back as 'rating' on POST /fin/csat.

label.description:
The human-readable label for this rating, localised to the conversation's
detected language. Distinct from 'key' — display the label, but send back
the key.

created_at_ms.description: The timestamp the event was created at, with millisecond precision.

rule_name.description: The rule's name as recorded when the consultation began, which may differ from its current name.

into.description: The number of tags the surviving contact already has.

from.description: The number of notes on the lead that would be reassigned to the surviving contact.

into.description: The number of notes the surviving contact already has.

operator.description:
The accepted operators you can use to define how you want to search for the value. Operator support depends on the field's data type. The breakdown below is for Contacts search; the other search endpoints that share this schema accept a different set per field:
- `string` fields: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `NIN`, `~`, `!~`, `^`, `$`
- `tag_id`: `=` and `!=` only. Every other operator returns an error.
- `boolean` fields: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `NIN`
- `integer` fields: `=`, `!=`, `IN`, `NIN`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`
- `datetime` fields (standard contact timestamps such as `created_at` and `last_seen_at`): `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`. Filtering is on the exact second, in UTC.
- `date` fields (Date custom attributes): `=`, `<`, `>` only. `!=`, `<=`, and `>=` are not supported and return an error. Values are truncated to a whole UTC day.

value.description: The value that you want to search on.

sla_applied.title: Applied SLA
sla_applied.description:
The SLA Applied object contains the details for which SLA has been applied to this conversation.
Important: if there are any canceled sla_events for the conversation - meaning an SLA has been manually removed from a conversation, the sla_status will always be returned as null.

sla_name.description: The name of the SLA as given by the teammate when it was created.

sla_status.description:
SLA statuses:
            - `hit`: If there’s at least one hit event in the underlying sla_events table, and no “missed” or “canceled” events for the conversation.
            - `missed`: If there are any missed sla_events for the conversation and no canceled events. If there’s even a single missed sla event, the status will always be missed. A missed status is not applied when the SLA expires, only the next time a teammate replies.
            - `active`: An SLA has been applied to a conversation, but has not yet been fulfilled. SLA status is active only if there are no “hit, “missed”, or “canceled” events.

name.description: The name of the company, used to look it up when neither `id` nor `company_id` is given.

companies.description: The id, company_id or name of the company can be passed as input parameters. Companies that cannot be found are skipped.

update_audience_request.title: Update Audience Request
update_audience_request.description: The request payload for updating an audience. All fields are optional — only provided fields will be updated.

predicates.description: The predicates that define which contacts belong to the audience.

role_predicates.description: Role-based predicates that further filter audience membership by contact role.

publish_article_draft_request.description:
Optional body for publishing a staged article draft. On a single-language
workspace the body can be omitted. On a multilingual workspace, `locales`
is required and lists which locales' drafts to publish.
publish_article_draft_request.title: Publish Article Draft Request Payload

locales.description:
The locales whose staged drafts should be published. Required on
multilingual workspaces; each locale must have a pending draft.

author_id.description: The id of the teammate to publish as. This is only used when the access token is not associated with a teammate, and is then required; omitting it returns 400 `parameter_not_found`. Otherwise the authenticating teammate is used. Must be a teammate on the workspace.

title.description: The title of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.

description.description: The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.

body.description:
The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`. Empty `

` tags are kept as blank paragraphs instead of being dropped.

body_markdown.description: The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

author_id.description: The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.

state.description: Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Omitting this field leaves the publish state unchanged, so a draft stays a draft and an edit to a published article goes live immediately unless that article already has a pending draft or a scheduled publish time is set in the same request. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.

parent_id.description: The id of the collection or section to move the article into. Omitting this field or sending `null` leaves the article's parent unchanged. Send `home` to remove the article from its collection so that it stands alone.

parent_ids.description: The ids of the parent collections to place this article in. Send an empty array to remove the article from all collections. When provided, this takes precedence over `parent_id`.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to remove it from its folder.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. Sending `audience_ids: []` clears all audience memberships from every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.

ai_chatbot_availability.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

scheduled_publish_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

scheduled_unpublish_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. The article must already be published; setting `state: "published"` in the same request does not count, and the request returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Combining with `state: "draft"` also returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. The value must be strictly in the future; timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid`. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

update_internal_article_request.title: Update Internal Article Request Payload

title.description: The title of the article.

body.description: The content of the article in HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.

body_markdown.description: The content of the article in markdown. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body` and `json_blocks`.

json_blocks.description: The content of the article as a list of content blocks. Used only when `body` is not provided. Cannot be combined with `body_markdown`. If none of `body`, `body_markdown` and `json_blocks` is provided, the existing content is kept.

locale.description: The locale of the article. If omitted, the existing locale is kept.

author_id.description: The id of the author of the article.

owner_id.description: The id of the author of the article.

folder_id.description: The ID of the folder to place this article in. Pass `null` to remove it from its folder. If omitted, the folder is unchanged.

audience_ids.description: The list of audience IDs to target this internal article to for Fin AI Agent. Omitting the field leaves existing audience memberships unchanged (PATCH semantics). Pass `[]` to clear all audience memberships. Unknown audience IDs return a `404` error with no partial commit.

ai_chatbot_availability.description: Whether the internal article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin).

ai_copilot_availability.description: Whether the internal article should be available for AI Copilot.

ai_sales_agent_availability.description: Whether the internal article should be available for AI Sales Agent.

name.description: The name of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the name of the default language's content.

description.description: The description of the collection. For multilingual collections, this will be the description of the default language's content.

icon.description: The icon of the collection, for example `book-bookmark`. If you leave out `icon`, or send it empty, the collection's icon is reset to `folder`.

parent_id.description: The id of the parent collection to move the collection into. Omitting this field or sending `null` leaves the collection where it is. Send `home` to move it to the first level.

help_center_id.description: Checked against the collection's Help Center but not applied, so it can't move the collection to another Help Center.

role.description: The role of the contact, either `user` or `lead`. Any other value is ignored. A user can't be changed to a lead; sending `lead` for a user returns a `400` error.

external_id.description: A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom

email.description: The contacts email

email_verified.description:
Whether the contact has proved they own this email address, for example through a confirmation link or one-time code you sent. Send it together with `email`. `email_verified` without `email` is rejected.

Changing a contact's email resets it to not verified. Intercom reuses leads with a verified email when an inbound email, conversation or ticket matches the address.

avatar.description: An image URL containing the avatar of a contact

signed_up_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.

last_seen_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).

owner_id.description: The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact

unsubscribed_from_emails.description: Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails

sms_consent.description: Whether the contact has consented to receive SMS messages.

unsubscribed_from_sms.description: Whether the contact is unsubscribed from SMS messages.

language_override.description: A preferred language setting for the contact, used by the Intercom Messenger even if their browser settings change.

custom_attributes.description: The custom attributes which are set for the contact

tags.name: AI Content
Auth Tokens
tags.description:
Read and write the third-party credentials stored in your workspace, so you can find the
id of the credential a data connector should authenticate with, and store a new one
without leaving your integration.
Reading requires an OAuth token with the `read_auth_tokens` scope; creating and updating
require the `write_auth_tokens` scope and an access token associated with a teammate.
You can create a `text` credential to send yourself, or an `oauth` credential whose
access token Intercom obtains and refreshes automatically via the client-credentials
grant. Only credentials with a `token_type` of `text` can be updated. No endpoint ever
returns a credential value, client secret, refresh configuration, or OAuth configuration.

Retrieve the banners a contact matches and record dismissals, so you can display
banners on surfaces outside the Messenger (native mobile apps, kiosks, embedded
tools). These endpoints require an OAuth token with the `read_write_users` scope.
Requesting a contact's banners records an impression for each banner returned, and
dismissals are shared with the web Messenger.
